c.tagline: Where the Red Sea meets the Horn of Africa's volcanic edge.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; agree the fare in Djiboutian francs with the driver before getting in. Shared taxis run fixed routes for a set per-seat price.

emergency.note: Bouffard French Military Hospital: +253 21 35 13 51; General Hospital Peltier: +253 21 35 27 12

hood_desc: Beachfront district on the Heron peninsula with the city's top luxury resort, embassies and calm sea views; suits travelers wanting comfort, pools and easy airport transfers.
Hillside diplomatic quarter overlooking the Gulf of Tadjoura, home to upscale hotels and foreign missions; suits business travelers and those wanting a quiet, secure base near downtown.

The historic colonial-grid downtown around Place du 27 Juin (Place Ménélik) with markets, cafes, government buildings and budget-to-midrange hotels; suits budget travelers and those wanting to walk to sights and the port.
A quieter residential municipality along the coast south of the center with a handful of independent hotels; suits travelers wanting a calmer, more local base still near downtown.
The functional strip near Djibouti-Ambouli Airport with simple business and transit hotels; suits overnight layovers, early flights or military/NGO logistics stays.

water.note: Tap water is not safe to drink; use bottled or boiled water.

transit.pay: City buses and shared taxis are paid in cash (Djiboutian francs) directly to the driver or conductor; there is no rechargeable transit card. The Addis Ababa-Djibouti train is booked and paid for at Nagad station in advance.
transit.hours: City buses and shared taxis run roughly 6am-8pm; private taxis available later but should be pre-arranged through a hotel at night.
transit.note: Djibouti City has no metro or tram; most visitors rely on taxis. Nagad station, 10km south of downtown, serves the twice-weekly Addis Ababa passenger train.

train: Ethio-Djibouti Railway from Nagad station to Addis Ababa via Dire Dawa
bus: Régie des Transports de Djibouti (RTD) city buses
Shared bush taxis/minibuses to Ali Sabieh, Dikhil, Tadjourah
ferry: Boat/dhow service to Moucha and Maskali islands

transit.m: Taxi (fixed/negotiated fare, no bus link to terminal)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or a small tip (5-10%) at hotels/restaurants is appreciated but not expected.
